base_instructions.text:
You are Codex, a coding agent based on GPT-5. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their goal is genuinely handled.

# Personality

You are a deeply pragmatic, effective software engineer. You take engineering quality seriously, and collaboration comes through as direct, factual statements. You communicate efficiently, keeping the user clearly informed about ongoing actions without unnecessary detail.

## Values
You are guided by these core values:
- Clarity: You communicate reasoning explicitly and concretely, so decisions and tradeoffs are easy to evaluate upfront.
- Pragmatism: You keep the end goal and momentum in mind, focusing on what will actually work and move things forward to achieve the user's goal.
- Rigor: You expect technical arguments to be coherent and defensible, and you surface gaps or weak assumptions politely with emphasis on creating clarity and moving the task forward.

## Interaction Style
You communicate respectfully, focusing on the task at hand. You always prioritize actionable guidance, clearly stating assumptions, environment prerequisites, and next steps.

You avoid cheerleading, motivational language, artificial reassurance, and general fluffiness. You don't comment on user requests, positively or negatively, unless there is reason for escalation.

## Escalation
You may challenge the user to raise their technical bar, but you never patronize or dismiss their concerns. When presenting an alternative approach or solution to the user, you explain the reasoning behind the approach, so your thoughts are demonstrably correct. You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.


# General
You bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. You read the codebase first, resist easy assumptions, and let the shape of the existing system teach you how to move.

- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.
- You parallelize tool calls whenever you can, especially file reads such as `cat`, `rg`, `sed`, `ls`, `git show`, `nl`, and `wc`. You use `multi_tool_use.parallel` for that parallelism, and only that. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo "====";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.

## Engineering judgment

When the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:

- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.
- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.
- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.
- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.
- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.

## Frontend guidance

You follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:

### Build with empathy
- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.
- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.
- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.
- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.

### Design instructions
- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.
- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.
- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.
- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.
- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.
- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.
- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.
- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.
- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.
- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. Primary images and media should reveal the actual product, place, object, state, gameplay, or person; you refrain from dark, blurred, cropped, stock-like, or purely atmospheric media when the user needs to inspect the real thing. For highly specific game assets you use custom SVG/Three.js/etc.
- For games or interactive tools with well-established rules, physics, parsing, or AI engines, you use a proven existing library for the core domain logic instead of hand-rolling it, unless the user explicitly asks for a from-scratch implementation.
- You use Three.js for 3D elements, and make the primary 3D scene full-bleed or unframed and not inside a decorative card/preview container. Before finishing, you verify with Playwright screenshots and canvas-pixel checks across desktop/mobile viewports that it is nonblank, correctly framed, interactive/moving, and that referenced assets render as intended without overlapping.
- You do not put UI cards inside other cards. Do not style page sections as floating cards. Only use cards for individual repeated items, modals, and genuinely framed tools. Page sections must be full-width bands or unframed layouts with constrained inner content.
- You do not add discrete orbs, gradient orbs, or bokeh blobs as decoration or backgrounds.
- You make sure that text fits within its parent UI element on all mobile and desktop viewports. Move it to a new line if needed, and if it still does not fit inside the UI element, use dynamic sizing so the longest word fits. Text must also not occlude preceding or subsequent content. Despite this, you check that text inside a UI button/card looks professionally designed and polished.
- Match display text to its container: reserve hero-scale type for true heroes, and use smaller, tighter headings inside compact panels, cards, sidebars, dashboards, and tool surfaces.
- You define stable dimensions with responsive constraints (such as  aspect-ratio, grid tracks, min/max, or container-relative sizing) for fixed-format UI elements like boards, grids, toolbars, icon buttons, counters, or tiles, so hover states, labels, icons, pieces, loading text, or dynamic content cannot resize or shift the layout.
- You do not scale font size with viewport width. Letter spacing must be 0, not negative.
- You do not make one-note palettes: avoid UIs dominated by variations of a single hue family, and limit dominant purple/purple-blue gradients, beige/cream/sand/tan, dark blue/slate, and brown/orange/espresso palettes; scan CSS colors before finalizing and revise if the page reads as one of these themes.
- You make sure that UI elements and on-screen text do not overlap with each other in an incoherent manner. This is extremely important as it leads to a jarring user experience.

When building a site or app that needs a dev server to run properly, you start the local dev server after implementation and give the user the URL so they can try it. If there's already a server on that port, you use another one. For a website where just opening the HTML will work, you don't start a dev server, and instead give the user a link to the HTML file that can open in their browser.

## Editing constraints

- You default to ASCII when editing or creating files. You introduce non-ASCII or other Unicode characters only when there is a clear reason and the file already lives in that character set.
- You add succinct code comments only where the code is not self-explanatory. You avoid empty narration like "Assigns the value to the variable", but you do leave a short orienting comment before a complex block if it would save the user from tedious parsing. You use that tool sparingly.
- Use `apply_patch` for manual code edits. Do not create or edit files with `cat` or other shell write tricks. Formatting commands and bulk mechanical rewrites do not need `apply_patch`.
- Do not use Python to read or write files when a simple shell command or `apply_patch` is enough.
- You may be in a dirty git worktree.
  * NEVER revert existing changes you did not make unless explicitly requested, since these changes were made by the user.
  * If asked to make a commit or code edits and there are unrelated changes to your work or changes that you didn't make in those files, you don't revert those changes.
  * If the changes are in files you've touched recently, you read carefully and understand how you can work with the changes rather than reverting them.
  * If the changes are in unrelated files, you just ignore them and don't revert them.
- While working, you may encounter changes you did not make. You assume they came from the user or from generated output, and you do NOT revert them. If they are unrelated to your task, you ignore them. If they affect your task, you work **with** them instead of undoing them. Only ask the user how to proceed if those changes make the task impossible to complete.
- Never use destructive commands like `git reset --hard` or `git checkout --` unless the user has clearly asked for that operation. If the request is ambiguous, ask for approval first.
- You are clumsy in the git interactive console. Prefer non-interactive git commands whenever you can.

## Special user requests

- If the user makes a simple request that can be answered directly by a terminal command, such as asking for the time via `date`, you go ahead and do that.
- If the user asks for a "review", you default to a code-review stance: you prioritize bugs, risks, behavioral regressions, and missing tests. Findings should lead the response, with summaries kept brief and placed only after the issues are listed. Present findings first, ordered by severity and grounded in file/line references; then add open questions or assumptions; then include a change summary as secondary context. If you find no issues, you say that clearly and mention any remaining test gaps or residual risk.

## Autonomy and persistence
You stay with the work until the task is handled end to end within the current turn whenever that is feasible. Do not stop at analysis or half-finished fixes. Do not end your turn while `exec_command` sessions needed for the user’s request are still running. You carry the work through implementation, verification, and a clear account of the outcome unless the user explicitly pauses or redirects you.

Unless the user explicitly asks for a plan, asks a question about the code, is brainstorming possible approaches, or otherwise makes clear that they do not want code changes yet, you assume they want you to make the change or run the tools needed to solve the problem. In those cases, do not stop at a proposal; implement the fix. If you hit a blocker, you try to work through it yourself before handing the problem back.

# Working with the user

You have two channels for staying in conversation with the user:
- You share updates in `commentary` channel.
- After you have completed all of your work, you send a message to the `final` channel.

The user may send messages while you are working. If those messages conflict, you let the newest one steer the current turn. If they do not conflict, you make sure your work and final answer honor every user request since your last turn. This matters especially after long-running resumes or context compaction. If the newest message asks for status, you give that update and then keep moving unless the user explicitly asks you to pause, stop, or only report status.

Before sending a final response after a resume, interruption, or context transition, you do a quick sanity check: you make sure your final answer and tool actions are answering the newest request, not an older ghost still lingering in the thread.

When you run out of context, the tool automatically compacts the conversation. That means time never runs out, though sometimes you may see a summary instead of the full thread. When that happens, you assume compaction occurred while you were working. Do not restart from scratch; you continue naturally and make reasonable assumptions about anything missing from the summary.

## Formatting rules

You are writing plain text that will later be styled by the program you run in. Let formatting make the answer easy to scan without turning it into something stiff or mechanical. Use judgment about how much structure actually helps, and follow these rules exactly.

- You may format with GitHub-flavored Markdown.
- You add structure only when the task calls for it. You let the shape of the answer match the shape of the problem; if the task is tiny, a one-liner may be enough. Otherwise, you prefer short paragraphs by default; they leave a little air in the page. You order sections from general to specific to supporting detail.
- Avoid nested bullets unless the user explicitly asks for them. Keep lists flat. If you need hierarchy, split content into separate lists or sections, or place the detail on the next line after a colon instead of nesting it. For numbered lists, use only the `1. 2. 3.` style, never `1)`. This does not apply to generated artifacts such as PR descriptions, release notes, changelogs, or user-requested docs; preserve those native formats when needed.
- Headers are optional; you use them only when they genuinely help. If you do use one, make it short Title Case (1-3 words), wrap it in **…**, and do not add a blank line.
- You use monospace commands/paths/env vars/code ids, inline examples, and literal keyword bullets by wrapping them in backticks.
- Code samples or multi-line snippets should be wrapped in fenced code blocks. Include an info string as often as possible.
- When referencing a real local file, prefer a clickable markdown link.
  * Clickable file links should look like [app.py](/abs/path/app.py:12): plain label, absolute target, with optional line number inside the target.
  * If a file path has spaces, wrap the target in angle brackets: [My Report.md](</abs/path/My Project/My Report.md:3>).
  * Do not wrap markdown links in backticks, or put backticks inside the label or target. This confuses the markdown renderer.
  * Do not use URIs like file://, vscode://, or https:// for file links.
  * Do not provide ranges of lines.
  * Avoid repeating the same filename multiple times when one grouping is clearer.
- Don’t use emojis or em dashes unless explicitly instructed.

## Final answer instructions

In your final answer, you keep the light on the things that matter most. Avoid long-winded explanation. In casual conversation, you just talk like a person. For simple or single-file tasks, you prefer one or two short paragraphs plus an optional verification line. Do not default to bullets. When there are only one or two concrete changes, a clean prose close-out is usually the most humane shape.

- You suggest follow ups if useful and they build on the users request, but never end your answer with an "If you want" sentence.
- When you talk about your work, you use plain, idiomatic engineering prose with some life in it. You avoid coined metaphors, internal jargon, slash-heavy noun stacks, and over-hyphenated compounds unless you are quoting source text. In particular, do not lean on words like "seam", "cut", or "safe-cut" as generic explanatory filler.
- The user does not see command execution outputs. When asked to show the output of a command (e.g. `git show`), relay the important details in your answer or summarize the key lines so the user understands the result.
- Never tell the user to "save/copy this file", the user is on the same machine and has access to the same files as you have.
- If the user asks for a code explanation, you include code references as appropriate.
- If you weren't able to do something, for example run tests, you tell the user.
- Never overwhelm the user with answers that are over 50-70 lines long; provide the highest-signal context instead of describing everything exhaustively.
- Tone of your final answer must match your personality.
- Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.

## Intermediary updates

- Intermediary updates go to the `commentary` channel.
- User updates are short updates while you are working, they are NOT final answers.
- You treat messages to the user while you are working as a place to think out loud in a calm, companionable way. You casually explain what you are doing and why in one or two sentences.
- Never praise your plan by contrasting it with an implied worse alternative. For example, never use platitudes like "I will do <this good thing> rather than <this obviously bad thing>", "I will do <X>, not <Y>".
- Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.
- You provide user updates frequently, every 30s.
- When exploring, such as searching or reading files, you provide user updates as you go. You explain what context you are gathering and what you are learning. You vary your sentence structure so the updates do not fall into a drumbeat, and in particular you do not start each one the same way.
- When working for a while, you keep updates informative and varied, but you stay concise.
- Once you have enough context, and if the work is substantial, you offer a longer plan. This is the only user update that may run past two sentences and include formatting.
- If you create a checklist or task list, you update item statuses incrementally as each item is completed rather than marking every item done only at the end.
- Before performing file edits of any kind, you provide updates explaining what edits you are making.
- Tone of your updates must match your personality.

- Dodao test koji pokriva scenario sa sekundarnim AS400 template-om: [JdbcTemplateConfigTest.java](</c:/Users/imijajlovic/Documents/workspaces/CBR/cbreporting-backend/src/test/java/rs/unicredit/cbr/config/JdbcTemplateConfigTest.java:21>).

payload.message:
Ne bi trebalo da poremeti postojeće ponašanje. Promena samo razdvaja dva `JdbcTemplate`-a:

- `jdbcTemplate` = glavni Oracle datasource iz `spring.datasource`
- `glFeePrepareDataJdbcTemplate` = AS400 datasource, samo za `GlFeePrepareDataService`

Do sada je problem mogao da nastane čim postoji custom AS400 `JdbcTemplate`: Spring Boot tada ne napravi automatski standardni Oracle `JdbcTemplate`, pa archive servis dobije AS400 template. Ova izmena eksplicitno vraća normalan Oracle `jdbcTemplate` i archive servisi ga traže po imenu.

To što je produkcija prazna nije bitno za ovu grešku. Pad se dešava na `connection.prepareCall(...)`, pre nego što procedura stvarno krene i pre bilo kakvog brojanja/redova. AS400 driver pokušava da pripremi poziv `CBR.SP_ARCHIVE_CBR_DATA` / `CBR.SP_ARCHIVE_GL_FEE_DATA`, što je Oracle procedura, i AS400 security/user-exit ga odbija.

Zašto dev nije pucao, a prod jeste: bug se aktivira samo ako su istovremeno uključeni archive scheduleri i postoji AS400 `glFeePrepareDataJdbcTemplate`. U prod yaml-u je `GL_FEE_PREPARE_DATA_ENABLED` default `false`, ali sam log dokazuje da je u runtime-u AS400 template postojao, što znači da je u prod okruženju verovatno env var postavljen na `true` ili je korišćen drugi profil/override. Dev možda nije imao isti override, nije radio u 02:00/04:00, ili su archive jobovi bili isključeni.

Verifikovao sam: `mvn test` prolazi, `114` testova. Also, pretragom koda jedini drugi AS400 `JdbcTemplate` korisnik već ima `@Qualifier("glFeePrepareDataJdbcTemplate")`, tako da mu ponašanje ostaje isto.

AS400 driver pokušava da pripremi poziv `CBR.SP_ARCHIVE_CBR_DATA` / `CBR.SP_ARCHIVE_GL_FEE_DATA`, što je Oracle procedura, i AS400 security/user-exit ga odbija.

Zašto dev nije pucao, a prod jeste: bug se aktivira samo ako su istovremeno uključeni archive scheduleri i postoji AS400 `glFeePrepareDataJdbcTemplate`. U prod yaml-u je `GL_FEE_PREPARE_DATA_ENABLED` default `false`, ali sam log dokazuje da je u runtime-u AS400 template postojao, što znači da je u prod okruženju verovatno env var postavljen na `true` ili je korišćen drugi profil/override. Dev možda nije imao isti override, nije radio u 02:00/04:00, ili su archive jobovi bili isključeni.

Verifikovao sam: `mvn test` prolazi, `114` testova. Also, pretragom koda jedini drugi AS400 `JdbcTemplate` korisnik već ima `@Qualifier("glFeePrepareDataJdbcTemplate")`, tako da mu ponašanje ostaje isto.

payload.message:
Koriste se ove 4 poslovne role:

```ts
ROLE_ADMIN: "App-CBR-ADMIN"
ROLE_SENIOR: "App-CBR-SENIOR"
ROLE_JUNIOR: "App-CBR-JUNIOR"
VIEWER_ROLE: "App-CBR-VIEWER"
```

Ne koristi se:

```ts
ROLE_USER: "App-CBR-USER"
```

U backend konfiguraciji nema `USER` mape. Postoje samo:

```yaml
roles:
  ADMIN:
    - App-CBR-ADMIN
  SENIOR:
    - App-CBR-SENIOR
  JUNIOR:
    - App-CBR-JUNIOR
  VIEW:
    - App-CBR-VIEWER
```

Bitna napomena: backend ne proverava nazive `ROLE_ADMIN`, `ROLE_SENIOR` itd. To su verovatno frontend konstante. Backend proverava Keycloak authority vrednosti, npr. `App-CBR-ADMIN`.

Većina akcija je dozvoljena za:

```text
ADMIN, SENIOR, JUNIOR
```

`VIEW` / `App-CBR-VIEWER` se koristi samo za read/view pristup na mestima gde je eksplicitno dodato, npr. auth/current-user i jedan lock view endpoint. Viewer ne može retry/enrich/calculate/booking akcije.

Za local/uat profil ekvivalenti su sa `UAT` sufiksom:

```text
App-CBR-ADMINUAT
App-CBR-SENIORUAT
App-CBR-JUNIORUAT
App-CBR-VIEWERUAT
```

Log potvrđuje regresiju koju sam upravo ispravio: `GlFeePrepareDataService` je išao na Oracle `jdbcTemplate`, ne na AS400. Zato piše:

```text
AS400 GET_FEEACCOUNT_IN failed ...
ORA-00904: "BEGPL"."GET_FEEACCOUNT_IN": invalid identifier
```

Da je stvarno išlo na AS400, ne bi dobio `ORA-*` grešku. Uzrok je bio `@Qualifier` na `final` field-u uz Lombok `@RequiredArgsConstructor`; Spring u runtime-u nije garantovano koristio taj qualifier na generisanom konstruktoru. Nakon što smo dodali primarni Oracle `jdbcTemplate`, ovaj servis je pokupio primarni Oracle template.

Ispravio sam:
- [GlFeePrepareDataService.java](</c:/Users/imijajlovic/Documents/workspaces/CBR/cbreporting-backend/src/main/java/rs/unicredit/cbr/service/GlFeePrepareDataService.java:47>) sada ima ručni konstruktor sa `@Qualifier("glFeePrepareDataJdbcTemplate")`.
- [JdbcTemplateConfigTest.java](</c:/Users/imijajlovic/Documents/workspaces/CBR/cbreporting-backend/src/test/java/rs/unicredit/cbr/config/JdbcTemplateConfigTest.java:36>) sada testira baš taj slučaj: Oracle primary + AS400 secondary, a `GlFeePrepareDataService` mora da dobije AS400 template.

Verifikacija: `mvn test` prolazi, `115` testova.

Ostali logovi su odvojeni problemi:
- `Current user lacks required roles`: korisnik nema `App-CBR-ADMIN`, `App-CBR-SENIOR` ili `App-CBR-JUNIOR`.
- `GSE MQ template is not configured`: aplikacija pokušava routing ka GSE, ali GSE MQ nije uključen/konfigurisan (`MQ_GSE_ENABLED` i povezani parametri).
- SpringDoc i Java agent warning nisu uzrok pada.

Posle deploy-a ovog fixa, redovi `feeDataId=334/335` koji su završili u `ENRICH_ERROR` treba da se retry-uju; tada bi `GET_FEEACCOUNT_IN` trebalo stvarno da ode na AS400.

sada je greska 2026-05-04T14:05:43.900+02:00 ERROR 1 --- [CBReportingApplication] [nio-8080-exec-3] r.u.cbr.service.GlFeeEnrichmentService : GL fee enrichment failed feeDataId=333 callReplyRef=1171265200233534: GET_FEEACCOUNT returned no rows for callReplyRef=1171265200233534
java.lang.IllegalStateException: GET_FEEACCOUNT returned no rows for callReplyRef=1171265200233534
at rs.unicredit.cbr.service.GlFeeEnrichmentService.extractSingleRow(GlFeeEnrichmentService.java:181) ~[!/:0.0.1-SNAPSHOT]

mozda funkcija stvarno ne vraca red.

Da, ova greška sada znači da poziv prolazi tehnički, ali funkcija stvarno vraća `0` redova.

Za `feeDataId=333` ranije si proverio:

```text
333  1171265200233534  OUT  ENRICH_ERROR
```

Znači pozvana je:

```sql
SELECT f.*
FROM TABLE(BEGPL.GET_FEEACCOUNT_OUT(CAST('1171265200233534' AS CHAR(16)))) f
```

Ovo više nije problem pogrešnog datasource-a. Da je i dalje išlo na Oracle, video bi `ORA-00904`. Da je AS400 odbio SQL, video bi JT400/AS400 SQL exception. Ovde nema SQL exception-a, nego naš kod dobije prazan `rows` i baci:

```text
GET_FEEACCOUNT returned no rows
```

Treba proveriti direktno na AS400/prod konekciji sa istim korisnikom i istim SQL-om:

```sql
SELECT f.*
FROM TABLE(BEGPL.GET_FEEACCOUNT_OUT(CAST('1171265200233534' AS CHAR(16)))) f
```

payload.message: greska u logu je: I/O error on POST request for "https://je6.uat.cee.intranet.unicreditgroup.eu/IHUBService5/EnterGLDealEntry.asmx": Connect timed out

To znači da aplikacija nije ni stigla do IHUB/GL booking servisa. Pao je TCP/HTTPS connect:

```text
Connect timed out
```

Dakle nije greška u payload-u, fee podacima ili statusu, nego mrežna dostupnost endpointa iz okruženja gde radi backend.

Endpoint iz loga je UAT:

```text
https://je6.uat.cee.intranet.unicreditgroup.eu/IHUBService5/EnterGLDealEntry.asmx
```

Proveri za produkciju da li stvarno treba UAT endpoint. U `application-prod.yaml` default je:

```yaml
customs.services.gl-booking.endpoint:
  https://je6.cee.intranet.unicreditgroup.eu/IHUBService5/EnterGLDealEntry.asmx
```

Ako u produkciji vidiš `je6.uat...`, onda env var override verovatno postavlja:

```text
GL_BOOKING_ENDPOINT=https://je6.uat.cee.intranet.unicreditgroup.eu/IHUBService5/EnterGLDealEntry.asmx
```

Provera na serveru/podu:

```bash
printenv | grep GL_BOOKING
```

Treba proveriti i mrežu iz poda:

```bash
curl -vk --connect-timeout 10 \
  https://je6.uat.cee.intranet.unicreditgroup.eu/IHUBService5/EnterGLDealEntry.asmx
```

Ako connect timeout ostane, treba mrežni/firewall/route/DNS pristup iz OpenShift namespace-a prema tom hostu/443. Nakon toga možeš retry booking za taj `callReplyRef`; status `BOOKING_ERROR` je baš za ovakav retry.

Kratko: nismo dodali posebnu kolonu tipa `SENT_TO_OM_GSE_AT` na transakciji. Datum slanja ka OM/GSE može da se izvede iz stage snapshot-a: poslednji ulazak u `S10`.

Za slanje ka OM/GSE gledaj:

```sql
select max(s.created_at) as sent_to_om_gse_at
  from cbr.tbl_cbr_stage_snapshot s
 where s.call_reply_ref = :call_reply_ref
   and s.to_stage_code = 'S10';
```

To je timestamp kada je CBR uspešno poslao MQ poruku i prebacio transakciju u `S10`.

**Datumi**
`Datum valute`:
- Kolona: `CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION.SETTLEMENT_DATE`
- Java polje: `settlementDate`
- P8/pacs.008: čitamo iz `GrpHdr/IntrBkSttlmDt`, fallback `CdtTrfTxInf/IntrBkSttlmDt`
- P4/pacs.004: čitamo iz `GrpHdr/IntrBkSttlmDt`
- Značenje: ISO settlement/value date iz payment poruke.

`Datum prijema` može značiti dve stvari:
- `CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION_REQUEST.RECEIVED_AT`: kada je CBR primio raw XML/MQ poruku i upisao request. Ovo je pravi CBR receive timestamp.
- `CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION.SOURCE_RECEIVED_AT`: timestamp iz same izvorne poruke. Za P8 uzimamo `CdtTrfTxInf/AccptncDtTm`, ako nema onda `GrpHdr/CreDtTm`; za P4 uzimamo `GrpHdr/CreDtTm`.

`Processing date`:
- Nemamo posebnu business kolonu `PROCESSING_DATE`.
- U praksi se najčešće koristi `CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION.CREATED_AT` kao vreme kada je CBR parsirao/upisao transakciju.
- `CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION.UPDATED_AT` je poslednja izmena transakcije, ne stabilan processing date.

Za audit statusa/slanja:
- `TBL_CBR_STAGE_SNAPSHOT.CREATED_AT` + `TO_STAGE_CODE`
- `S10` = poslato OM/GSE
- `S4` = poslato Skipper-u
- `S9` = response pripremljen za slanje

Ako treba tačan SQL za jedan nalog:

```sql
select t.call_reply_ref,
       t.settlement_date        as datum_valute,
       r.received_at            as cbr_datum_prijema,
       t.source_received_at     as datum_iz_izvorne_poruke,
       t.created_at             as cbr_processing_time,
       t.updated_at             as last_update_time,
       (select max(s.created_at)
          from cbr.tbl_cbr_stage_snapshot s
         where s.cbr_transaction_id = t.id
           and s.to_stage_code = 'S10') as sent_to_om_gse_at
  from cbr.tbl_cbr_transaction t
  join cbr.tbl_cbr_transaction_request r on r.id = t.request_id
 where t.call_reply_ref = :call_reply_ref;
```

```bash
GL_FEE_PREPARE_DATA_ENABLED=true
```

Za GL fee flow kompletno treba:

- dodat je `CorsFilter` na najvišem prioritetu.

Verifikacija: `mvn test "-Dtest=JdbcTemplateConfigTest"` prolazi.

Posle deploy-a proveri iz browsera ili curl-om:

```bash
curl -i -X OPTIONS \
  'https://cbreporting-backend.hvbyu.com/api/outgoing/get-all' \

  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: GET' \

```

Treba da vidiš:

```text
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://universe.hvbyu.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```

payload.message: ali kod mene se otvaraju podaci na frontendu dok kod kolege imamovu gresku? zasto?

Ako tebi radi, a kolegi ne, backend CORS najverovatnije više nije osnovni problem. Razlika je u tome kakav request kolegin browser šalje ili šta dobija od autentikacije/proxy-ja.

Najčešći uzrok: kolega nema validan JWT token u requestu. Ranije si već imao odgovor:

```json
"JWT token nedostaje..."
```

Kada token fali ili je istekao, browser može prikazati CORS ako 401 odgovor/proxy odgovor ne sadrži CORS header.

Neka kolega proveri u DevTools -> Network za `/api/outgoing/get-all`:
- `Request Headers` -> da li postoji `Authorization: Bearer ...`
- `Origin` -> mora biti `https://universe.hvbyu.com`
- `Status Code` -> da li je `401`, `403`, `302`, `0`, ili nešto drugo
- `Response Headers` -> da li ima `access-control-allow-origin`

Razlike koje mogu objasniti:
- Kolega nije ulogovan ili mu je token istekao.
- Kolega ima stare frontend assete u cache-u/service worker-u.
- Kolega pristupa preko drugog URL-a/origina, npr. `http`, drugi hostname, ili stari Universe URL.
- Kolega nema role `App-CBR-ADMIN/SENIOR/JUNIOR/VIEWER`, pa dobija auth error.
- Browser extension/security policy blokira header.
- Load balancer još šalje deo saobraćaja na staru backend repliku.

Brzi koraci za kolegu:
1. Hard refresh: `Ctrl+F5`.
2. Logout/login u Universe.
3. Incognito prozor.
4. Clear site data za `https://universe.hvbyu.com`.
5. U Network tabu proveriti da li `Authorization` postoji.

Ako kolega pošalje screenshot Network detalja za jedan failed request, posebno `Request Headers`, `Status Code` i `Response Headers`, može se tačno videti da li je auth, cache, origin ili stari pod.

content.text: koliko kb tokena moze da prodje kroz browser

payload.message: koliko kb tokena moze da prodje kroz browser

Nema jedne browser granice samo za JWT. Praktična granica je zbir svih HTTP header-a koje prihvataju browser, proxy/ingress, load balancer i backend.

Tipične granice:

```text
Pojedinačni header: često oko 8 KB
Ukupni request headers: često 8 KB, 16 KB ili 32 KB
Cookie header: često problem već oko 4 KB po cookie-ju ili 8 KB ukupno
```

JWT ide u:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Ako je token 6-8 KB, već možeš imati problem na proxy/ingress sloju, naročito ako uz to ide i `Cookie` header. Kod kolege se vidi veliki `Authorization` header + cookie + ostali browser header-i. Ako proxy ima limit 8 KB ukupno, može vratiti `400 Bad Request` pre aplikacije, baš kao na screenshot-u.

Praktično:
- do `2-4 KB` token je uglavnom bez problema
- `5-8 KB` je rizično
- preko `8 KB` često puca na proxy/load balanceru
- preko `16 KB` je vrlo verovatno problem u enterprise okruženjima

Za proveru dužine tokena u konzoli browsera:

```js
const token = localStorage.getItem("access_token");
token?.length
```

Ako token nije u `localStorage`, u Network tabu može da se kopira vrednost `Authorization` header-a i izmeri dužina.

U njegovom slučaju bih proverio:
1. dužinu JWT tokena
2. da li token sadrži previše rola/grupa
3. da li se šalju nepotrebni cookies ka `cbreporting-backend.hvbyu.com`
4. limit ingress/proxy-ja za request headers, npr. 8 KB/16 KB.

content.text: koji propusta maksimalnu velicinu headera koji browser?

payload.message: koji propusta maksimalnu velicinu headera koji browser?

Ne bira browser “maksimalnu veličinu headera” u praksi. Limit najčešće postavlja prvi server/proxy ispred aplikacije:

```text
Browser -> Ingress/Router/WAF/Load balancer -> Spring Boot backend
```

Ako dobiješ `400 Bad Request` sa `text/html`, to skoro sigurno nije Spring Boot nego ingress/proxy.

Tipični limiti:
- NGINX/Ingress: često oko `8 KB` po headeru ili po bufferu
- HAProxy/OpenShift router: često limitira ukupnu veličinu HTTP request headera
- Tomcat/Spring Boot: može se podešavati sa `server.max-http-request-header-size`

Za Spring Boot možeš povećati:

```yaml
server:
  max-http-request-header-size: 32KB
```

Ali ako OpenShift/ingress odbija pre aplikacije, ovo neće pomoći. Tada treba povećati limit na router/ingress/WAF sloju.

Browseri:
- Chrome/Edge/Firefox uglavnom nisu prvi limit za normalan JWT.
- Problem nastaje kada `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` + `Cookie` + ostali headeri pređu limit proxy-ja.
- Ako jedan korisnik ima mnogo rola/grupa u JWT-u, njegov token može biti mnogo veći od tvog.

Praktično proveri kod kolege:
```js
[...document.cookie].length
```

i dužinu tokena ako je u storage-u:

```js
localStorage.getItem("access_token")?.length
```

Ako je JWT preko ~8 KB, traži smanjenje claims/roles u tokenu ili povećanje header limita na ingress/proxy sloju.

Ovo je skoro sigurno probijen header limit na proxy/ingress/nginx sloju, ne u browseru.

Razlog: request se vidi u Network tabu i dobija:

```text
400 Bad Request
content-type: text/html;charset=utf-8
```

Znači browser ga je poslao. Spring backend najverovatnije nije ni dobio request. Tvoj `Authorization: Bearer ...` je ogroman jer JWT sadrži stotine rola u `realm_access.roles`.

Prvi `get-all` koji vrati `200` je verovatno prošao sa manjim/drugačijim headerima ili iz drugog momenta, a naredni request sa punim tokenom i cookies prelazi limit.

**Kako potvrditi**
1. Pogledaj `Response` tab za taj `400`. Verovatno piše nešto kao:
```text
Request Header Or Cookie Too Large
Bad Request
```

2. Proveri backend log u isto vreme. Ako nema loga za `/api/incoming/get-all`, request je pao pre aplikacije.

3. Izmeri token:
```js
const h = '<kopiran ceo Authorization header>';
h.length
```

Kod ovog korisnika token deluje mnogo veći od 8 KB, moguće 15-25 KB.

**Pravo rešenje**
Smanjiti JWT u Keycloak-u. CBR backend koristi samo:

```text
App-CBR-ADMIN
App-CBR-SENIOR
App-CBR-JUNIOR
App-CBR-VIEWER
```

Nema potrebe da token nosi sve ove ostale grupe/role. U Keycloak klijentu za Universe/CBR treba isključiti full realm roles u access tokenu ili podesiti client scope/mappere da šalju samo CBR role.

Privremeno rešenje je povećati header limit na nginx/ingress/router sloju, npr. na 32 KB ili 64 KB, ali bolje je smanjiti token. Spring `server.max-http-request-header-size` neće pomoći ako nginx odbija pre aplikacije.

payload.message: da li mogu iz cmd?

Može iz CMD/PowerShell, ali moraš prvo imati token u fajlu ili clipboard-u. Pošto je token ogroman, najlakše je preko clipboard-a.

U PowerShell-u:

```powershell
(Get-Clipboard).Length
```

Koraci:
1. U browser Network tabu kopiraj ceo token ili ceo `Authorization` header.
2. Otvori PowerShell.
3. Pokreni:

```powershell
(Get-Clipboard).Length
```

Ako si kopirao ceo header sa `Bearer `, rezultat uključuje i tih 7 karaktera. To je ok.

Ako želiš da meriš samo token bez `Bearer `:

```powershell
$h = Get-Clipboard
$h = $h -replace '^Bearer\s+', ''
$h.Length
```

Može i iz CMD-a, ali PowerShell je mnogo jednostavniji za ovo.

payload.message: gde da unesem ovu komandu u console?

Tu si na pravom mestu. Dole levo vidiš plavi prompt:

```text
>
```

Ali Chrome te prvo blokira zbog paste zaštite. Uradi ovako:

1. U taj red pored `>` upiši tačno:

```text
allow pasting
```

2. Pritisni Enter.

3. Onda možeš da nalepiš komandu, npr:

```js
const token = `OVDE_NALEPI_TOKEN`;
token.length
```

Ako si kopirao ceo `Authorization` header sa `Bearer ...`, koristi:

```js
const h = `OVDE_NALEPI_CEO_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER`;
h.length
```

Nemoj slati token ovde u chat. Samo nam javi broj koji dobiješ.

- prvi request možda prođe
- sledeći sa dodatnim cookies/cache-control/headerima pređe limit
- proxy/ingress vrati `400 Bad Request text/html`
- browser to prikaže kao CORS jer nema `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`

Ovo treba rešiti jednim od ova dva načina:

1. Bolje rešenje: smanjiti JWT u Keycloak-u  
   Token sada nosi gomilu rola. CBR koristi samo:
   ```text

   App-CBR-SENIOR
   App-CBR-JUNIOR
   App-CBR-VIEWER
   ```
   Treba podesiti client scope/mappers da u access token ne ulaze sve realm role/grupe, nego samo CBR role.

2. Privremeno rešenje: povećati header limit na ingress/nginx/router sloju  
   Tražiti npr. `32 KB` ili `64 KB` max request headers. Spring Boot podešavanje neće pomoći ako proxy odbija pre aplikacije.

Možeš dodatno potvrditi: neka kolega izbriše cookies za `hvbyu.com` i proba incognito. Ako počne da radi, token+cookies zbir prelazi limit.

content.text: koliko je rizicno na backendu i frontendu da to menjam ?

payload.message: koliko je rizicno na backendu i frontendu da to menjam ?

Ako misliš na povećanje header limita: rizik za backend/frontend kod je mali, jer se kod ne menja. Rizik je infrastrukturni: veći header limit dopušta veće requeste kroz proxy, što može povećati memorijsku potrošnju po konekciji i malo proširiti DoS površinu. Povećanje na `16 KB` ili `32 KB` je obično prihvatljivo; `64 KB` bih koristio samo ako mora.

Ako misliš na smanjenje JWT-a: to je bolje dugoročno, ali funkcionalno rizičnije ako druge aplikacije u Universe portalu zavise od svih tih rola u tokenu. Za CBR backend nije rizično ako ostanu samo CBR role koje koristimo: `App-CBR-ADMIN`, `App-CBR-SENIOR`, `App-CBR-JUNIOR`, `App-CBR-VIEWER`.

Za CBR frontend rizik je mali ako frontend samo prosleđuje token i prikazuje UI po CBR rolama. Rizik postoji ako frontend negde očekuje druge role/claims iz tog istog tokena.

Moj pragmatičan redosled:
1. Kratkoročno povećati ingress/proxy header limit na `16 KB` ili `32 KB`, da produkcija radi.
2. Dugoročno srediti Keycloak mapper/client scope da CBR dobija manji token samo sa relevantnim rolama.
3. Ne povećavati limit previše kao trajno rešenje, jer token od 8 KB je već signal da se u JWT šalje previše nepotrebnih claims.

Backend Spring promena `server.max-http-request-header-size` ima smisla samo ako request stiže do aplikacije. Kod vas `400 text/html` ukazuje da puca pre backenda, pa treba infrastruktura/proxy.

payload.message:
milsio sam koliko je rizicno Dugoročno srediti Keycloak mapper/client scope da CBR dobija manji token samo sa relevantnim rolama.

treba i backend da menjam?

Za CBR backend najverovatnije ne treba menjati kod, ako Keycloak i dalje šalje CBR role u tokenu pod istim claim-om.

Backend trenutno čita role iz:

```json
realm_access.roles
```

i uzima samo one koje počinju sa:

```text
App-CBR-
```

Dakle backendu je dovoljno da u tokenu ostanu:

```text
App-CBR-ADMIN
App-CBR-SENIOR
App-CBR-JUNIOR
App-CBR-VIEWER
```

Rizik je nizak ako se promena radi samo za CBR/Universe client scope tako da:
- iz tokena izbaciš nepotrebne role
- ostaviš CBR role u `realm_access.roles`
- ne promeniš naziv rola
- ne prebaciš role u drugi claim bez dogovora

Rizik postaje srednji/visok ako:
- isti Keycloak client `myApp` koriste i druge aplikacije koje očekuju sve realm role
- ukloniš `realm_access.roles` kompletno
- CBR role prebaciš u `resource_access.myApp.roles`, a ne ostaviš ih u `realm_access.roles`
- frontend koristi druge role iz tokena za meni/permission logiku

Backend već delimično čita i client role iz:

```json
resource_access.myApp.roles
```

ali tu ne filtrira samo `App-CBR-`. Ipak, autorizacija radi preko tačnih vrednosti iz konfiguracije, pa bi prošlo i ako su `App-CBR-*` tamo. Ali da se izbegne rizik, najbolje je ostaviti `App-CBR-*` u `realm_access.roles`.

Preporuka za bezbednu promenu:
1. Napraviti poseban client scope/mapper za CBR.
2. U token ubacivati samo `App-CBR-*` role.
3. Testirati sa jednim korisnikom koji ima `ADMIN/SENIOR/JUNIOR/VIEWER`.
4. Proveriti `/api/auth/me` ili current-user endpoint da vraća očekivane role.
5. Tek onda primeniti šire.

Dakle: backend ne treba menjati ako claim ostane kompatibilan. Treba samo pažljivo podesiti Keycloak da ne polomi druge aplikacije koje dele isti client/token.

payload.message: ja sve to mogu da uradim u frontendu app?

Ne u potpunosti. Frontend ne može stvarno da smanji JWT koji je već izdao Keycloak. Token sadržaj se određuje na Keycloak strani, kroz client scopes/mappers/roles.

Frontend može samo:
- da prestane da šalje token na endpoint-e kojima ne treba auth
- da ne šalje nepotrebne custom header-e
- da izbegne slanje cookies ako nisu potrebni
- eventualno da koristi drugi token ako Keycloak izda manji token za drugi client/scope

Ali frontend ne može bezbedno “iseći” JWT i poslati manju verziju, jer bi se potpis pokvario. Backend bi odbio takav token.

Za tvoju situaciju:
- `/api/outgoing/get-all` i `/api/incoming/get-all` traže auth, tako da frontend mora poslati `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Ako je token 8133 karaktera, problem se rešava u Keycloak-u ili na proxy/header limitu, ne u frontend kodu.

Frontend može pomoći privremeno ako ukloni nepotrebne cookies ka backendu. Ako axios/fetch šalje `withCredentials: true`, a backend ne koristi cookies, možeš ga isključiti:

```js
axios.defaults.withCredentials = false
```

ili za API client:

```js
axios.create({
  baseURL: "...",
  withCredentials: false,
})
```

Ali glavni problem je ogroman JWT. Dugoročno: Keycloak mapper/client scope. Kratkoročno: povećanje ingress/proxy header limita.

payload.message:
Da, to se radi u Keycloak-u na nivou **client-a / client scope-a**, ne u frontend aplikaciji.

Najbezbedniji princip: ne dirati globalno realm role za sve aplikacije, nego ograničiti role samo za client koji koristi CBR/Universe.

U Keycloak Admin Console traži ovako:

1. Izaberi realm, kod vas verovatno `Universe`.
2. Idi na `Clients`.
3. Otvori client koji frontend koristi, po tokenu izgleda da je:
   ```text
   azp = myApp
   ```
4. Na client-u nađi podešavanje:
   ```text
   Full Scope Allowed
   ```
   i postavi na `OFF`.

5. Zatim idi na tab:
   ```text
   Client scopes
   ```
   ili u novijem Keycloak-u:
   ```text
   Client details -> Dedicated scopes
   ```

6. U `Scope` / `Role scope mappings` dodaj samo role koje smeju u token:
   ```text
   App-CBR-*
   CLM-*
   ```
   Keycloak UI obično ne radi wildcard `*` kao filter, nego moraš dodati konkretne role ili composite role.

Najbolja varijanta je da napraviš composite role, npr:

```text
CBR_ACCESS
CLM_ACCESS
```

i u njih ubaciš konkretne role:

```text
App-CBR-ADMIN
App-CBR-SENIOR
App-CBR-JUNIOR
App-CBR-VIEWER
CLM-...
```

Pa client scope mapira samo te composite role.

Važno: Keycloak obično neće “regex filtrirati” realm roles po prefiksu `CBR.*` / `CLM.*` kroz standardni UI. Standardan način je:
- `Full Scope Allowed = OFF`
- eksplicitno dodate role u role scope mappings
- ili composite role koje sadrže željene role

Posle promene koristi `Evaluate`:
1. `Clients -> myApp`
2. `Client scopes` / `Evaluate`
3. Izaberi korisnika
4. Generate access token
5. Proveri da `realm_access.roles` više ne sadrži sve role, nego samo CBR/CLM role.

CBR backend ne mora da se menja ako u tokenu ostanu `App-CBR-*` role u `realm_access.roles`.

Keycloak dokumentacija baš za ovo kaže da se role u tokenu mogu ograničiti preko role scope mappings i da se kroz client scopes/evaluate može videti efektivan token. Izvor: Keycloak Server Administration Guide, sekcije za client scopes i role scope mappings: https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/

payload.message: ne nalazim  Full Scope Allowed

U ovoj starijoj Red Hat SSO/Keycloak konzoli to nije na `Client Scopes` tabu. Idi ovako:

1. `Clients` -> `myApp`
2. Tab `Scope` gore, ne `Client Scopes`
3. Tu bi trebalo da vidiš `Full Scope Allowed` toggle/checkbox.
4. Isključi ga.
5. Ispod u `Realm Roles` / `Client Roles` dodeli samo role koje token sme da dobije.

Za CBR backend mora da ostane bar:

```text
App-CBR-ADMIN
App-CBR-SENIOR
App-CBR-JUNIOR
App-CBR-VIEWER
```

Ako želiš i CLM, dodaš i njihove role. Ako UI nema wildcard tipa `CBR.*`, mora ručno ili preko composite role, npr. napraviš composite `App-CBR-ACCESS` koji sadrži CBR role, pa njega dodeliš u scope.

Posle toga proveri u `Client Scopes` -> `Evaluate`: izaberi korisnika, generiši token i gledaj da li je `realm_access.roles` mnogo kraći, ali da i dalje sadrži `App-CBR-*` role. Backend ne mora da se menja ako te role ostanu u tokenu pod istim nazivima.

payload.message: ovde?

Da, ovo je globalni `roles` client scope, ali ne bih prvo dirao njega ako `myApp` koriste i druge aplikacije.

Ovde vidiš bitno: `Include In Token Scope = OFF`. To znači da ovaj scope verovatno nije direktno uzrok što su sve role u access tokenu, nego role najverovatnije ulaze preko client scope mapper-a ili preko `Full Scope Allowed` na klijentu.

Idi ovako:

1. Vrati se na `Clients` -> `myApp`.
2. Otvori tab `Scope`.
3. Tu traži `Full Scope Allowed`.
4. Ako postoji, stavi `OFF`.
5. U istom tabu dodaj samo potrebne role u scope mappings:
   `App-CBR-ADMIN`, `App-CBR-SENIOR`, `App-CBR-JUNIOR`, `App-CBR-VIEWER`.

Ako ne nalaziš `Full Scope Allowed` ni na `Clients -> myApp -> Scope`, onda proveri ovde gde si sada:

1. `Client Scopes` -> `roles`
2. Tab `Mappers`
3. Nađi mapper koji puni `realm_access.roles` ili `resource_access.*.roles`
4. Tu se vidi da li dodaje sve realm role u token.

Nemoj gasiti/brisati globalni `roles` scope na slepo, jer može da skrati tokene za sve aplikacije u realm-u, ne samo za CBR.

Da, ovo je globalni `roles` client scope, ali ne bih prvo dirao njega ako `myApp` koriste i druge aplikacije.

Ovde vidiš bitno: `Include In Token Scope = OFF`. To znači da ovaj scope verovatno nije direktno uzrok što su sve role u access tokenu, nego role najverovatnije ulaze preko client scope mapper-a ili preko `Full Scope Allowed` na klijentu.

Idi ovako:

1. Vrati se na `Clients` -> `myApp`.
2. Otvori tab `Scope`.
3. Tu traži `Full Scope Allowed`.
4. Ako postoji, stavi `OFF`.
5. U istom tabu dodaj samo potrebne role u scope mappings:
   `App-CBR-ADMIN`, `App-CBR-SENIOR`, `App-CBR-JUNIOR`, `App-CBR-VIEWER`.

Ako ne nalaziš `Full Scope Allowed` ni na `Clients -> myApp -> Scope`, onda proveri ovde gde si sada:

1. `Client Scopes` -> `roles`
2. Tab `Mappers`
3. Nađi mapper koji puni `realm_access.roles` ili `resource_access.*.roles`
4. Tu se vidi da li dodaje sve realm role u token.

Nemoj gasiti/brisati globalni `roles` scope na slepo, jer može da skrati tokene za sve aplikacije u realm-u, ne samo za CBR.

payload.message:
`BOOKED` scheduler je neće pokupiti dok je `ENRICHED`. Tok je:

```text
ENRICHED
  -> GlFeeCalculationScheduler
  -> calculate fee + prepare booking data
  -> PREPARED
  -> GlFeeBookingExecutionScheduler
  -> BOOKED / BOOKING_ERROR
```

Ako ostaje u `ENRICHED`, najverovatnije je calculation scheduler našao red, ali nije našao nijedno pravilo u `TBL_CBR_FEE_MATRIX`. Kod u tom slučaju namerno ostavlja status `ENRICHED` i samo piše WARN:

```text
GL fee calculation left row in ENRICHED because no rule matched ...
```

Proveri prvo log na produkciji za:

```text
callReplyRef=1271265240009502
GL fee calculation left row in ENRICHED
GL fee calculation scheduler finished prepared=
```

Najbrža provera je da ručno pozoveš calculate endpoint za tu referencu:

```text
POST /api/gl-fee-calculation/1271265240009502
```

Ako vrati:

```text
No fee matrix rule matched callReplyRef=1271265240009502
```

onda nije scheduler problem, nego fee matrix ne pokriva tu kombinaciju.

Pusti i ovaj SQL:

```sql
SELECT
    g.id,
    g.call_reply_ref,
    g.booking_status,
    g.message_type,
    g.direction,
    g.segment,
    g.creditor_agent,
    g.debtor_lrc,
    g.creditor_lrc,
    g.cr_statistical_code,
    g.amount,
    g.amount_rsd,
    g.middrate,
    g.sdc,
    g.ref,
    g.debit_account,
    g.credit_account,
    g.fee,
    g.applied_fee_rule_no,
    g.status_updated_at,
    g.updated_by
FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA g
WHERE g.call_reply_ref = '1271265240009502';
```

Zatim vidi kandidatska pravila:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_MATRIX m
WHERE m.active = 'Y'
  AND m.message_type = (
      SELECT g.message_type
      FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA g
      WHERE g.call_reply_ref = '1271265240009502'
  )
  AND m.direction = (
      SELECT g.direction
      FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA g
      WHERE g.call_reply_ref = '1271265240009502'
  )
  AND (m.valid_from IS NULL OR m.valid_from <= TRUNC(SYSDATE))
  AND (m.valid_to IS NULL OR m.valid_to >= TRUNC(SYSDATE))
ORDER BY m.priority, m.id;
```

Ako ručni calculate uspe, red će otići u `PREPARED`, pa ga onda booking scheduler treba pokupiti u sledećem ciklusu. Ako ostane `PREPARED`, onda gledamo `CBR_FEE_EXECUTE_PREPARED_ENABLED` i booking log/error.

Scheduler je verovatno pokupio red, ali ga namerno ostavlja u `ENRICHED` jer nema matching fee pravilo.

Tvoj red:

```text
call_reply_ref = 1271265240009502
status         = ENRICHED
message_type   = P8
direction      = INT
segment        = PI
debtor_lrc     = 50060
creditor_lrc   = 50060
amount         = 1 EUR
amount_rsd     = 117.39
sdc            = 60
ref            = 6324200001
```

Kandidatska pravila koja postoje za `P8/INT` su:

```text
rule 11: P8 INT SEGMENT_PI + LRC_OSIGURANJE
rule 12: P8 INT SEGMENT_PI + LRC_HUMANITARNA
```

A tvoja transakcija ima `50060 / 50060`. `50060` nije osiguranje/humanitarna lista, nego po seed podacima spada u `LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA`. Zato nijedno od ta dva pravila ne prolazi i kod ostavlja red u `ENRICHED`.

Proveri liste:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_RULE_ITEM
WHERE list_code IN ('LRC_OSIGURANJE', 'LRC_HUMANITARNA', 'LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA')
ORDER BY list_code, sort_order, id;
```

Ako poslovno pravilo kaže da se `P8 INT / PI / 50060` naplaćuje, treba dodati ili izmeniti rule u `CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_MATRIX`, npr. pravilo za:

```text
MESSAGE_TYPE = P8
DIRECTION = INT
SEGMENT_LIST_CODE = SEGMENT_PI
DEBTOR_LRC_LIST_CODE ili CREDITOR_LRC_LIST_CODE = LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA
AMOUNT_CCY = EUR
FEE_MODE = PERCENT
...
```

Ne treba ručno prebacivati u `PREPARED`, jer tada još nisu popunjeni `fee`, `credit_account`, `narrative1`, `applied_fee_rule_no`. Kada rule bude pokrio red, calculation scheduler će ga prebaciti u `PREPARED`. Za `sdc=60` credit account mapping postoji u kodu, tako da sledeći potencijalni blocker nije tu.

payload.message:
Za `clientContract = NE` nismo poslali samu referencu `1171265250009503` contract servisu. Referenca služi samo da nađemo transakciju. Contract servis dobija `clientId` izveden iz računa.

Logika je:

```text
DIRECTION = IN   -> šalje creditor_account_no
DIRECTION = OUT  -> šalje debtor_account_no
DIRECTION = INT  -> prvo creditor_account_no, zatim debtor_account_no
```

Za svaki account radi se:

```java
digits = account.replaceAll("\\D", "")
clientId = digits / 1000
clientId = left-pad na 8 cifara
```

Payload ka contract-status servisu je:

```json
{
  "requestHeader": {
    "userId": "...",
    "opu": "...",
    "sourceApp": "CBR",
    "requestCode": "<uuid>"
  },
  "clientId": "<izvedenih 8 cifara>"
}
```

U prod konfiguraciji URL je:

```text
https://wso2gw.hvbyu.com/cbr/2.0/client/v1/contract-status
```

Da vidiš tačno šta je otišlo za `1171265250009503`, pusti:

```sql
SELECT
    t.id,
    t.request_id,
    t.call_reply_ref,
    t.direction,
    t.debtor_account_no,
    t.debtor_agent,
    t.creditor_account_no,
    t.creditor_agent,
    t.client_contract
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION t
WHERE t.call_reply_ref = '1171265250009503';
```

Ako je `OUT`, poslali smo clientId izveden iz `DEBTOR_ACCOUNT_NO`.
Ako je `IN`, iz `CREDITOR_ACCOUNT_NO`.
Ako je `INT`, pozvana su oba, a drugi poziv za `DEBTOR_ACCOUNT_NO` može da pregazi vrednost iz prvog jer se `client_contract` upisuje u isto polje.

U logu bi trebalo da postoji linija:

```text
Contract-status mapping for requestId=<request_id> account=<account> clientContract=NE
```

To je najtačniji dokaz koji account je poslat.

Iz reda se vidi približno:

```text
call_reply_ref = 1171265250009505
message_type   = P8
direction      = OUT
segment        = SME pravno lice-Retail
debtor_lrc     = 504306
creditor_agent = BPMOIT22XXX
amount         = 2932 EUR
amount_rsd     = 344165.49
sdc            = 31
booking_status = ENRICHED
```

Za `P8 / OUT / SME` trenutno mogu da prođu ova pravila:

```text
rule 6  -> SEGMENT_SME + FLASH_BIC
rule 7  -> SEGMENT_SME + LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA + amount_rsd < 2.500.000
rule 8  -> SEGMENT_SME + LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA + amount_rsd 2.500.000 - 5.000.000
rule 9  -> SEGMENT_SME + LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA + amount_rsd > 5.000.000
rule 10 -> SEGMENT_SME + CR_STATISTICAL_CODE = 103
```

Kod ove transakcije:

```text
BPMOIT22XXX nije u FLASH_BIC
504306 nije u LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA
CR_STATISTICAL_CODE nije 103
```

Zato calculation scheduler ne nalazi pravilo i namerno ostavlja red u `ENRICHED`.

Proveri konkretno:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_RULE_ITEM
WHERE item_value IN ('504306', 'BPMOIT22XXX')
ORDER BY list_code, sort_order;
```

Ako poslovno `504306` treba da se tretira kao “sopstvena sredstva” za SME, treba ga dodati u listu `LRC_SOPSTVENA_SREDSTVA`. Tada bi ova transakcija upala u rule 7, jer je `amount_rsd = 344165.49`, ispod `2.500.000 RSD`.

Ako nije sopstvena sredstva, treba dodati/korigovati fee matrix rule za `P8 OUT SME` i taj LRC.

payload.message:
Prebacivanje kandidata za fee je urađeno u dva koraka.

**1. Transakcija prvo dobija `FEE_STATUS = READY`**

To se radi posle uspešnog slanja poruke u eksterni MQ, tj. posle S10 flow-a. Kod izračuna:

```text
READY   ako je kandidat za fee
SKIPPED ako nije kandidat
```

Kriterijum za kandidata je:

```text
MESSAGE_TYPE mora biti P8
```

i onda po smeru:

```text
OUT -> uvek kandidat

IN  -> kandidat samo ako je segment PI

INT -> kandidat samo ako je segment PI
```

Segment se uzima ovako:

```text
prvo DEBTOR_SEGMENT ako postoji,
inače CREDITOR_SEGMENT
```

Za `IN` postoji i ranije markiranje na `READY` odmah posle creditor enrichment-a ako je:

```text
MESSAGE_TYPE = P8
DIRECTION = IN
CREDITOR_SEGMENT = PI
```

**2. Scheduler prebacuje `READY` iz transakcije u `TBL_GL_FEE_DATA`**

Scheduler `GlFeeReadyTakeScheduler` uzima samo transakcije gde je:

```text
FEE_STATUS = READY
MESSAGE_TYPE = P8
DIRECTION IN (OUT, INT, IN)
FEE_READY_AT <= now - readyDelayMinutes
```

Default delay je 10 minuta:

```text
customs.fee-booking.take-ready.ready-delay-minutes: 10
```

Zatim još jednom radi zaštitnu proveru istog eligibility pravila. Ako prođe, upisuje red u `CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA` sa:

```text
BOOKING_STATUS = NEW
```

i originalnu transakciju označava:

```text
FEE_STATUS = TAKEN
```

Ako za isti `CALL_REPLY_REF` već postoji red u `TBL_GL_FEE_DATA`, ne pravi duplikat, nego samo označi transakciju kao `TAKEN`.

Bitno: u ovoj logici nema provere fee matrix pravila. To znači da kandidat može ući u `TBL_GL_FEE_DATA`, dobiti `ENRICHED`, pa tek kasnije ostati u `ENRICHED` ako fee matrix ne pokriva tu kombinaciju.

payload.message:
Za ove dve reference najbrže je da pogledaš STP log, jer backend tamo čuva tačan razlog.

Pusti:

```sql
WITH last_log AS (
    SELECT l.*,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.request_id ORDER BY l.run_no DESC) rn
      FROM CBR.TBL_STP_VALIDATION_LOG l
)
SELECT
    t.call_reply_ref,
    t.request_id,
    t.customer_stp,
    t.message_type,
    t.direction,
    t.report_type,
    t.client_contract,
    t.payment_instrument,
    t.special_mark,
    t.creditor_country,
    t.debtor_country,
    LISTAGG(s.split_stat_code, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.id) AS split_stat_codes,
    l.success AS stp_success,
    DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(l.stp_result_json, 4000, 1) AS stp_result_json
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION t
LEFT JOIN CBR.TBL_CBR_TRANSACTION_STAT s
       ON s.call_reply_ref = t.call_reply_ref
LEFT JOIN last_log l
       ON l.request_id = t.request_id
      AND l.rn = 1
WHERE t.call_reply_ref IN ('1171265250010025', '1171265250010015')
GROUP BY
    t.call_reply_ref,
    t.request_id,
    t.customer_stp,
    t.message_type,
    t.direction,
    t.report_type,
    t.client_contract,
    t.payment_instrument,
    t.special_mark,
    t.creditor_country,
    t.debtor_country,
    l.success,
    DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(l.stp_result_json, 4000, 1);
```

Za `P8 OUT/INT` STP prolazi samo ako je sve ovo OK:

```text
REPORT_TYPE = 70
CLIENT_CONTRACT = Y
svi SPLIT_STAT_CODE su u dozvoljenoj OUT listi
PAYMENT_INSTRUMENT = 1
SPECIAL_MARK je null ili 0/1/3
CREDITOR_COUNTRY nije XK
```

Izuzetak: ako je `REPORT_TYPE = 66`, kod ga automatski pušta kao STP.

U `stp_result_json` ćeš dobiti nešto kao:

```json
{
  "manualRequired": true,
  "failures": [
    { "code": "CLIENT_CONTRACT", "message": "Ugovor (NE)" }
  ]
}
```

Kodovi znače:

```text
REPORT_TYPE        -> reporting type nije 70
CLIENT_CONTRACT    -> ugovor nije Y
SPLIT_STAT_CODE    -> statistički kod nije u STP dozvoljenoj listi
PAYMENT_INSTRUMENT -> instrument nije 1
SPECIAL_MARK       -> posebna oznaka nije prazna/0/1/3
CREDITOR_COUNTRY   -> creditor country je XK
DEBTOR_COUNTRY     -> debtor country je XK, za IN
```

Pošalji rezultat ovog SQL-a i mogu ti tačno reći za obe reference koji uslov ih je izbacio iz STP-a.

Tačno:

```java
RULE5_ALLOWED_SPLIT_STAT_CODES
```

sadrži `895`:

```text
...,701,699,707,341,895,702,340,...
```

To je lista za matrix/business validaciju, koristi se kod rule 5 provere, oko:

```java
RULE5_ALLOWED_SPLIT_STAT_CODES.contains(...)
```

Ali STP za `OUT/INT` koristi drugu listu:

```java
STP_ALLOWED_SPLIT_STAT_CODES_OUT
```

```java
STP_ALLOWED_SPLIT_STAT_CODES_IN

```

```text
895 prolazi opštu validaciju rule 5
895 ne prolazi STP validaciju
```

payload.message: daj mi uslove koje stavljamo u  ready a koje u skipped za FEE?

Za `FEE_STATUS` trenutno važi ovo:

```text
READY  = kandidat za fee
SKIPPED = nije kandidat za fee
```

Status se postavlja posle uspešnog slanja poruke ka eksternom sistemu, tj. posle S10.

**READY uslovi**

Transakcija dobija `FEE_STATUS = READY` ako je:

```text
MESSAGE_TYPE = P8
```

i jedan od sledećih uslova:

```text
DIRECTION = OUT
```

ili:

```text
DIRECTION = IN
segment = PI
```

ili:

```text
DIRECTION = INT
segment = PI
```

Segment se računa ovako:

```text
segment = DEBTOR_SEGMENT ako postoji
inače CREDITOR_SEGMENT
```

Za `IN` postoji i ranije markiranje u `READY` odmah posle creditor enrichment-a ako je:

```text
MESSAGE_TYPE = P8
DIRECTION = IN
CREDITOR_SEGMENT = PI
```

**SKIPPED uslovi**

Transakcija dobija `FEE_STATUS = SKIPPED` ako ne zadovolji gore navedeno, konkretno:

```text
MESSAGE_TYPE nije P8
```

ili:

```text
DIRECTION nije OUT, IN, INT
```

ili:

```text
DIRECTION = IN ili INT
segment nije PI
```

Za `OUT` se ne proverava segment: svaki `P8 OUT` ide u `READY`.

Posle toga scheduler uzima samo:

```text
FEE_STATUS = READY
MESSAGE_TYPE = P8
DIRECTION IN (OUT, IN, INT)
FEE_READY_AT <= now - readyDelayMinutes
```

i prebacuje ih u `TBL_GL_FEE_DATA`.

payload.message:
Za `1171265250010032` je najverovatnije isto: enrichment je uspeo, ali fee calculation nije našao matching rule u `TBL_CBR_FEE_MATRIX`, pa ga namerno ostavlja u `ENRICHED`.

Pusti prvo ovaj SQL:

```sql
SELECT
    g.id,
    g.request_id,
    g.call_reply_ref,
    g.booking_status,
    g.message_type,
    g.direction,
    g.segment,
    g.debtor_lrc,
    g.creditor_lrc,
    g.creditor_agent,
    g.cr_statistical_code,
    g.amount,
    g.amount_rsd,
    g.middrate,
    g.sdc,
    g.ref,
    g.debit_account,
    g.credit_account,
    g.fee,
    g.applied_fee_rule_no,
    g.status_updated_at,
    g.updated_by
FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA g
WHERE g.call_reply_ref = '1171265250010032';
```

Onda kandidatska pravila za isti `message_type/direction`:

```sql
SELECT
    m.rule_no,
    m.rule_name,
    m.active,
    m.priority,
    m.message_type,
    m.direction,
    m.segment_list_code,
    m.flash_list_code,
    m.debtor_lrc_list_code,
    m.creditor_lrc_list_code,
    m.cr_statistical_code,
    m.amount_ccy,
    m.amount_from,
    m.amount_to,
    m.fee_mode,
    m.fee_rate,
    m.fee_fix_amount,
    m.fee_min,
    m.fee_max
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_MATRIX m
WHERE m.active = 'Y'
  AND m.message_type = (
      SELECT g.message_type
      FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA g
      WHERE g.call_reply_ref = '1171265250010032'
  )
  AND m.direction = (
      SELECT g.direction
      FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA g
      WHERE g.call_reply_ref = '1171265250010032'
  )
  AND (m.valid_from IS NULL OR m.valid_from <= TRUNC(SYSDATE))
  AND (m.valid_to IS NULL OR m.valid_to >= TRUNC(SYSDATE))
ORDER BY m.priority, m.id;
```

Ako hoćeš direktno da vidiš koji uslov pada po pravilu:

```sql
WITH g AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM CBR.TBL_GL_FEE_DATA
    WHERE call_reply_ref = '1171265250010032'
)
SELECT
    m.rule_no,
    m.rule_name,
    CASE
      WHEN m.segment_list_code IS NULL THEN 'OK'
      WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_RULE_ITEM i
          WHERE i.list_code = m.segment_list_code
            AND i.active = 'Y'
            AND UPPER(TRIM(i.item_value)) = UPPER(TRIM((SELECT segment FROM g)))
      ) THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'FAIL segment'
    END AS segment_check,
    CASE
      WHEN m.debtor_lrc_list_code IS NULL THEN 'OK'
      WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_RULE_ITEM i
          WHERE i.list_code = m.debtor_lrc_list_code
            AND i.active = 'Y'
            AND UPPER(TRIM(i.item_value)) = UPPER(TRIM((SELECT debtor_lrc FROM g)))
      ) THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'FAIL debtor_lrc'
    END AS debtor_lrc_check,
    CASE
      WHEN m.creditor_lrc_list_code IS NULL THEN 'OK'
      WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_RULE_ITEM i
          WHERE i.list_code = m.creditor_lrc_list_code
            AND i.active = 'Y'
            AND UPPER(TRIM(i.item_value)) = UPPER(TRIM((SELECT creditor_lrc FROM g)))
      ) THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'FAIL creditor_lrc'
    END AS creditor_lrc_check,
    CASE
      WHEN m.flash_list_code IS NULL THEN 'OK'
      WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_RULE_ITEM i
          WHERE i.list_code = m.flash_list_code
            AND i.active = 'Y'
            AND UPPER(TRIM(i.item_value)) = UPPER(TRIM((SELECT creditor_agent FROM g)))
      ) THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'FAIL flash'
    END AS flash_check,
    CASE
      WHEN m.cr_statistical_code IS NULL THEN 'OK'
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(m.cr_statistical_code)) = UPPER(TRIM((SELECT cr_statistical_code FROM g))) THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'FAIL cr_statistical_code'
    END AS stat_check
FROM CBR.TBL_CBR_FEE_MATRIX m
WHERE m.active = 'Y'
  AND m.message_type = (SELECT message_type FROM g)
  AND m.direction = (SELECT direction FROM g)
ORDER BY m.priority, m.id;
```

Pošalji rezultat prvog i trećeg upita, pa ću ti tačno reći koje pravilo je trebalo da ga pokupi i šta ga blokira.

imam problem sa prevelikom tokenom

Da, ovo sada više nije nagađanje: zahtev stiže do Spring Boot/Tomcat-a i Tomcat ga odbija pre nego što Security/CORS/JWT obrada uopšte krene.

Greška:

```text
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Request header is too large
```

znači da su ukupni request header-i preveliki, najviše zbog `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`. Ranije si izmerio token oko `8133` karaktera, a sa `Bearer `, cookies i ostalim browser headerima pređe default limit.

Kratkoročni fix na backendu:

```yaml
server:
  max-http-request-header-size: 32KB
```

ili preko env var:

```text
SERVER_MAX_HTTP_REQUEST_HEADER_SIZE=32KB
```

Ako imate nginx/ingress ispred aplikacije, tamo takođe mora limit da bude veći, npr. 16K ili 32K. Ali ovaj konkretan log je iz Tomcat-a, znači backend limit sigurno treba povećati.

Dugoročno bolje rešenje je Keycloak: smanjiti access token da ne nosi sve realm role korisnika, nego samo role relevantne za CBR. Backend trenutno treba samo `App-CBR-*` role, ne ceo spisak svih AD/realm grupa.

payload.message: imam backend i frontend. gde bi trebao da bude nginx

`nginx` bi trebalo da bude **ispred backenda**, na putanji kojom browser zove API.

Tipičan raspored:

```text
Browser
  -> frontend domen / portal
  -> backend API domen
      -> nginx / ingress / route / load balancer
          -> Spring Boot backend
```

Za tvoj problem sa velikim JWT headerom bitni su svi slojevi kroz koje prolazi API request:

```text
Browser
  -> nginx/ingress/router
  -> Spring Boot Tomcat
```

Limit mora biti dovoljno velik na oba mesta:

1. Na `nginx` / ingress / OpenShift route / reverse proxy sloju
2. U Spring Boot backendu:

```yaml
server:
  max-http-request-header-size: 32KB
```

Ako frontend samo servira statičke fajlove, njegov nginx nije glavni problem osim ako isti nginx proxy-pass-uje `/api` ka backendu.

Kod tebe zahtev ide direktno na:

```text
https://cbreporting-backend.hvbyu.com/api/...
```

Znači limit tražiš na infrastrukturi za `cbreporting-backend.hvbyu.com`, ne na frontend aplikaciji.

content.text: kako da proverim da li imam nginx na backendu?

payload.message: kako da proverim da li imam nginx na backendu?

Najbrže proveri iz 3 ugla.

**1. Po response headerima**

U browser DevTools -> Network -> klikni API request -> Headers -> Response Headers.

Traži nešto od ovoga:

```text
server: nginx
server: openresty
via: ...
x-forwarded-*
x-envoy-*
```

Ako dobiješ `server: nginx`, imaš nginx ispred ili kao ingress.

Možeš i iz terminala:

```powershell
curl.exe -I https://cbreporting-backend.hvbyu.com/api/outgoing/get-all
```

ili za bilo koji endpoint koji postoji.

**2. Po OpenShift/Kubernetes objektima**

Ako je backend na OpenShift-u, proveri:

```bash
oc get route
oc describe route cbreporting-backend
oc get ingress
oc describe ingress <name>
```

Ako vidiš `route`, ispred aplikacije je OpenShift router/HAProxy. Ako vidiš `ingress`, često iza toga može biti nginx ingress controller, ali zavisi od platforme.

Proveri i servise/podove:

```bash
oc get svc
oc get pods
```

Ako vidiš podove tipa:

```text
nginx-ingress
ingress-nginx-controller
router
haproxy
```

onda ima proxy sloj.

**3. Po tome gde nastaje greška**

Ovaj log:

```text
org.apache.coyote.http11.Http11Processor
Request header is too large
```

je iz Spring Boot embedded Tomcat-a. To znači da je zahtev prošao sve proxy slojeve ispred i stigao do backenda, pa ga je Tomcat odbio.

Dakle čak i ako postoji nginx/router, trenutno sigurno moraš povećati i backend limit:

```yaml
server:
  max-http-request-header-size: 32KB
```

Ako posle toga dobiješ 400/431 bez backend loga, onda je sledeći limit na proxy/ingress/router sloju.

Ima Tomcat lokalno, samo nije instaliran kao poseban server.

Spring Boot web aplikacija po default-u koristi **embedded Tomcat**. To je ovaj dependency/log:

```text
tomcat-embed-core-10.1.48.jar
org.apache.coyote.http11.Http11Processor
```

Znači lokalno request dolazi do embedded Tomcat-a u tvojoj Spring Boot aplikaciji i on odbija header:

```text
Request header is too large
```

Na serveru kažeš da request ni ne dođe do backenda. To znači da tamo puca ranije, na nekom sloju ispred aplikacije:

```text
Browser
  -> ingress / route / reverse proxy / load balancer
  -> backend Spring Boot embedded Tomcat
```

Lokalno imaš samo:

```text
Browser
  -> Spring Boot embedded Tomcat
```

Zato lokalno vidiš Tomcat grešku, a na serveru ne.

Za server treba proveriti infrastrukturni sloj za:

```text
https://cbreporting-backend.hvbyu.com
```

Ako je OpenShift, verovatno je:

```text
OpenShift Route / HAProxy router
```

Ako je Kubernetes ingress, može biti:

```text
nginx ingress / HAProxy / F5 / neki API gateway
```

Backend fix i dalje ima smisla:

```yaml
server:
  max-http-request-header-size: 32KB
```

ali za server moraš dodatno povećati limit na ruti/ingress/proxy-ju, jer zahtev ne stiže do aplikacije.

payload.message:
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-05T13:30:19.582595400Z",
  "message": "JWT token je nevažeći ili je istekao.",
  "status": 401,
  "path": "/api/cbr/mq/probe/skipper/inbound"
} da li mogu produkcioni token da koristim na localhostu

Ne, ne pouzdano. Produkcioni token možeš koristiti na localhostu samo ako lokalni backend koristi isti Keycloak issuer i isti realm kao produkcija.

Tvoj prod token je iz prod issuer-a:

```text
https://keycloak-rh-sso.apps.openshiftprod.hvbyu.com/auth/realms/Universe
```

A lokalni profil kod tebe verovatno koristi UAT/dev issuer:

```text
https://keycloak-rh-sso.apps.openshiftdev.hvbyu.com/auth/realms/automatauniverse
```

Spring JWT validacija poredi `iss` iz tokena sa `issuer-uri` iz konfiguracije. Ako se ne poklapaju, dobijaš:

```text
JWT token je nevažeći ili je istekao.
```

Možeš proveriti lokalni config:

```yaml
spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri
```

Ako hoćeš da lokalno koristiš produkcioni token, pokreni lokalni backend sa prod issuer/jwk configom, npr. env override:

```text
SPRING_SECURITY_OAUTH2_RESOURCESERVER_JWT_ISSUER_URI=https://keycloak-rh-sso.apps.openshiftprod.hvbyu.com/auth/realms/Universe
SPRING_SECURITY_OAUTH2_RESOURCESERVER_JWT_JWK_SET_URI=https://keycloak-rh-sso.apps.openshiftprod.hvbyu.com/auth/realms/Universe/protocol/openid-connect/certs
```

Ali pazi: time lokalno validiraš prod identitet/role. Za normalan lokalni rad bolje koristi token iz istog UAT/dev Keycloak realm-a koji je podešen u `application-local.yaml`.
